events.text: Summary of changes:**
Package 1 — Static security analysis in CI**
Added a new `static-analysis` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs Semgrep with the `p/javascript`, `p/nodejs`, and `p/security-audit` rule packs on every pull request and push to `main`.
Package 2 — Dangerous HTML sinks**

`src/intel/index.js`: Changed the `el()` helper's `innerHTML = html` to `textContent = text` (the html parameter was never actually passed by any call site — dead code path — so this is safe and removes the raw sink).

`src/shell/index.js`: Replaced `node.innerHTML = html` in the `el()` helper with a `DOMParser`-based approach (`parseFromString` → `append` from body child nodes), avoiding any direct `innerHTML` assignment while preserving identical DOM output from the static SVG/HTML strings that callers supply.
`src/shell/welcome.js`: Replaced `root.innerHTML = \`...\`` with a `DOMParser`-based approach for the same reason; all interpolated values are internal constants (no user data).
Package 3 — HTTPS enforcement**
`config/cctv_sources.warendorf.json`: Upgraded the Warendorf webcam URLs from `http://` to `https://`.
`server/providers/cctv/constants.js`: Updated `WARENDORF_IMAGE_ORIGINS` allowlist to `https://webcam.warendorf.de/`.
`server/providers/metar.js`: Changed dummy URL-parsing base from `'http://local'` to `'https://localhost'`.
`server/providers/terrain.js`: Changed dummy URL-parsing base from `'http://internal'` to `'https://localhost'`.
`server/providers/cctv/sources.js`: Removed bare `http://` from a JSDoc comment.
`build/vite.js`: Added `'Strict-Transport-Security': 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains'` to `PAGE_HEADERS` so the HSTS header is sent on every response.
Package 4 — Data protection notes**

Created `docs/DATA-PROTECTION.md` documenting all data classes (public-feed, aggregated-track, camera-media, simulated, user-interaction, operational-config), their storage locations, retention periods, personal-data handling, sensitive-aggregate guidance, encryption posture, and a review schedule.

FINISHED 4

# Data Protection Notes

This document records the personal and sensitive data that God's Eye View handles,
where it is stored, and how long it is kept.  It is maintained as the authoritative
data-classification record for ASVS V14 compliance (V14.1.1 / V14.1.2).

---

## 1. Data Classification

| Class | Description | Examples | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **public-feed** | Live telemetry from open, publicly broadcast sources | ADS-B aircraft positions, AIS vessel positions, satellite TLEs, USGS earthquake events, NASA FIRMS fire detections, METAR weather reports | Public |
| **aggregated-track** | Historical position sequences derived from public feeds | Reconstructed flight paths, voyage routes | Aggregated-sensitive — may be restricted for defence/government customers |
| **camera-media** | JPEG frames and HLS segments from public CCTV cameras | Traffic cameras (TfL, Transport for NSW, Calgary), municipal webcams (Warendorf, Tarktee) | Public — but frames may incidentally capture individuals in a public place |
| **simulated** | Synthetic entities used in Exercise or demo mode | Scripted aircraft, vessels and alerts | Internal/non-operational |
| **user-interaction** | Search queries entered in the place-search box | Free-text location strings | Transient — processed in-process only, never logged or persisted |
| **operational-config** | API keys, tokens and environment variables | Cesium ion token, Google Maps API key, OpenSky credentials | Secret — handled via environment variables; never included in build artefacts or logs |

---

## 2. Storage Locations and Retention

| Data Class | Storage Location | Retention Period | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| public-feed (aircraft, vessels, satellites, quakes, fires) | Browser memory only (client-side state) | Session lifetime — discarded on page close | No server-side persistence |
| public-feed (METAR weather) | Server in-memory Map (per-process) | ≤ 10 minutes (TTL-evicted); bounded to `STATIONS_MAX` entries | Not written to disk |
| public-feed (terrain heights) | Server in-memory Map + optional disk file (`config/terrain_heights.json`) | In-memory: session lifetime; disk file: manual update by operator | Disk file contains no personal data (grid elevation values) |
| aggregated-track | Browser memory only | Session lifetime | If a customer exports data via the CSV sheet, that export is the customer's responsibility |
| camera-media (JPEG frames) | Proxied through server with `Cache-Control: no-store`; held in memory for the duration of a single relay request | < 1 second (request lifetime) | No frame is written to disk; upstream cache headers are forwarded |
| camera-media (HLS segments) | Server in-memory segment ring buffer per active session | < 60 seconds (bounded ring; oldest segment evicted when ring fills) | No subprocess, no disk writes, no idle sweep |
| simulated | Browser memory only | Session lifetime | |
| user-interaction (place search) | Forwarded to Google Places API on behalf of the client; not logged or stored by this application | Zero — not retained | Google Places API terms apply to the forwarded query |
| operational-config | Process environment (`process.env`) | Process lifetime | Never written to logs or included in error responses sent to clients |

---

## 3. Personal Data Handling

God's Eye View does not collect, store or process personal data as a primary
function.  No user accounts, authentication sessions, cookies or device identifiers
are created or stored.

Camera frames from public CCTV cameras may incidentally capture individuals in
public spaces.  These frames are:

- Never stored beyond the duration of a single proxied request (JPEG) or a
  short HLS segment ring (< 60 s);
- Served with `Cache-Control: no-store` to prevent downstream caching;
- Sourced only from publicly accessible cameras operated by transport authorities
  and municipalities.

---

## 4. Sensitive Aggregated Data

When the platform is used to track military or government-restricted assets, the
aggregated position tracks visible in the browser session may be considered
operationally sensitive.  Operators in such environments must:

- Apply network-level controls so only authorised users can reach the application;
- Not export track data to unclassified systems;
- Apply applicable data-handling regulations (e.g. UK JSP 440, US NIST 800-53)
  at the organisational level.

---

## 5. Encryption and Integrity

- All external API calls made by the server use HTTPS (enforced in code).
- The application instructs browsers to enforce HTTPS via the
  `Strict-Transport-Security` response header (`max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`).
- No sensitive data is Base64-encoded or otherwise lightly obscured; secrets are
  kept in environment variables outside the application source tree.

---

## 6. Review Schedule

This document must be reviewed and updated whenever a new external data source,
persistent store, or user-data processing step is added to the application.
The designated reviewer is the project security lead.
